question.worked_solution:
Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$  

In the given congruence, we have $a=22$ and $n=51$, where

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(22,51)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $22\,(\text{mod}\,51).$ To find the inverse of $22\,(\text{mod}\,51)$, use the extended Euclidean algorithm.

First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}51 & = & 22\cdot 2 & + & 7 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 22 & = & 7\cdot 3 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the rightmost terms in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}7 & =51-22\cdot 2 \\ 1 & =22-7\cdot 3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =22-7\cdot 3 \\  & =22-(51-22\cdot 2)\cdot 3 \\  & =22\cdot 7+51\cdot (-3)\end{aligned}
$$

We can write this result in modulo $51,$ as follows:  

$$
\begin{aligned}22\cdot 7+51\cdot (-3) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ 22\cdot 7 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,51)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $22\cdot 7≡1\,(\text{mod}\,51),$ which means that $7$ is the multiplicative inverse of $22$ (modulo $51$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our original congruence by $7,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}22x & ≡5 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ 7\cdot 22x & ≡7\cdot 5 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ (7\cdot 22)x & ≡35 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡35 &  & (\text{mod}\,51) \\ x & ≡35 &  & (\text{mod}\,51)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡35\,(\text{mod}\,51).$
